# Part 1: Template test [12 min]{.time} {#part-1}

::: notes
**Goal.** Every participant leaves part 1 with their own numbers: both columns filled, at least one content fix in each round, and one sentence on what the template changed.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 12 minutes, shared on your screen, with the time typed into the chat at each cue. The lab page and Case A open in two tabs. Your own Rounds A and B, run once beforehand; never quote your numbers as typical, because the site has no such figure. Questions come in through the chat: answer in one line and keep the clock moving.

**Clock.** 0:00 set-up. 1:30 Round A. 6:00 say "New chat" and start Round B. 10:30 fill the table and write one sentence. 11:40 time.

**Watch for.** A result read as "the tool is so much better": there is no such number, and the numbers are theirs. A real patient detail in a chat: say the privacy line once, no shaming. Part 1 running over: shorten question two's independent check in part 2 from two minutes to one; never cut the save step or the debrief.

**Bridge.** "Time. Part 2: break it on purpose."
:::

## Set up: one case, two chats {#p1-setup}

- **One case:** the Case A facts block, the same in both rounds.
- **Two fresh chats**, one per round, in the same tool.
- **First draft only:** no re-prompting.
- **Four counts per round:** minutes, words, edits, and errors (invented, omitted, altered).

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 1 min 30 sec]{.tag} Copy the facts block and the worksheet into your notes.
:::

::: {.small .muted}
Lab page: [the facts](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#the-facts), [how to measure](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#how-to-measure-same-for-both-rounds), [the worksheet](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#worksheet)
:::

::: notes
**1:30.** One case, two chats, one stopwatch. Both rounds use the same facts block, which is Case A, a fictional patient, in two fresh chats of the same tool. Take the first draft only: you are measuring one prompt against the other, so no re-prompting. For each round record four things: minutes from Enter to a note you would sign, words in the first draft, edits, and errors, sorted as invented, omitted or altered. Copy the facts block and the worksheet into your notes now; the worksheet is at the end of the lab page.

**Do.** Start the 12-minute countdown as this slide appears. Paste the lab page link in the chat again. Answer questions in one line.
:::

# Part 2: Break it on purpose [8 min]{.time} {#part-2}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone sees once, safely, how confident a wrong answer sounds, runs the three questions on it, and saves it with its warning line for Lab Three.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 8 minutes. The lab page open at part 2. Your own probe, run beforehand, so you know what a confident wrong answer looks like in this tool today.

**Clock.** 0:00 the aim, then pick and run a probe. 3:00 the three questions, with two minutes to find one item. 6:30 save. 7:40 time.

**Watch for.** Probe five answered fluently and trusted: the lesson is that fluency told them nothing, only the check did. The saved wrong answer losing its header line: it must never pass for a right one. A tool that declines: that is a good answer; note it, push once, then try another probe.

**Bridge.** "Time. Part 3: the same question, two ways of answering."
:::

## Pick one probe and run it {#p2-probe}

[See how confident a wrong answer sounds.]{.big}

- Pick one of the five probes. Paste it into a new chat.
- Fill the brackets from your own field.
- Probe 5, the drug interaction, is the riskiest: pick a less common pair you know well, and never act on the output.
- If the tool declines, note it, then push once.

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 3 min]{.tag} Run your probe. [Lab page, part 2](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#part-2)
:::

::: notes
**3:00.** Ask a tool for something it cannot reliably know, and watch how it answers. The aim is not to catch the tool out; it is to see, once and safely, how confident a wrong answer sounds. Pick one of the five probes on the lab page and run it in a new chat in your general assistant. Fill the brackets from your own field, so you can judge the answer. Probe five, the drug interaction, is the highest-risk: choose a less common pair you know well, and never act on the output. If the tool declines, that is a good answer: note it, then push once, as a busy colleague might.

**Do.** Say the time left at two minutes and one minute. Watch the chat; if someone's tool declined twice, suggest another probe.
:::

## Run the three questions {#p2-check}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[1]{.num}

**Could I defend this to a colleague?**
:::
::: {.card .teal}
[2]{.num}

**Does it point to something I can verify?**

Pick one item: a number, a paper or a date. Look for it for two minutes.
:::
::: {.card}
[3]{.num}

**Would I catch it if it were wrong?**

Would you have noticed, had you not looked?
:::
:::

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 3 min 30 sec]{.tag} Run the check on your answer. [Lab page, the check](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#run-the-check-then-save-it)
:::

::: notes
**3:30.** Run the three questions on the answer you got, in these words. Could I defend this to a colleague? Does it point to something I can verify? Would I catch it if it were wrong? For question two, pick one specific item, a number, a paper or a date, and try to find it independently for two minutes. For question three, ask whether you would have noticed had you not looked. Write your yes or no for each in the worksheet.

**Do.** Say "start looking" at the top of the two minutes, and again at the end. Watch the chat for the first "I could not find it"; thank them aloud: that is the lab working.
:::

## Save it with the warning line {#p2-save}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Save the answer in a note titled `lab1-practice-output`, with this line above it:

> **PRACTICE OUTPUT: CONTAINS DELIBERATELY UNRELIABLE CONTENT. NOT FOR CLINICAL USE.**
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.card .teal}
[What good looks like]{.t}

The header line, the answer, one item you tried to verify, and under it: the probe, what you found, and a verdict (trust, verify first, or discard).
:::
:::
:::

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 1 min 10 sec]{.tag} Save it. Lab Three reuses it. [Lab page, save it](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#run-the-check-then-save-it)
:::

::: notes
**1:10.** Save the answer in a note titled lab1-practice-output, with this exact line above it, so a saved wrong answer can never pass for a right one. Under the answer add one line: which probe you used and what you found when you checked, and then your verdict: trust, verify first, or discard. Good looks like this: one saved answer with the header line, one item you tried to verify, and a verdict. If your tool declined and the push did not help, try another probe. Lab Three reuses this note.

**Do.** Read the header line aloud, word for word, and paste it into the chat so people can copy it. Do not discuss the answers yet; the debrief comes at the end. Say "Time." at 7:40.
:::

# Part 3: Tool face-off [5 min]{.time} {#part-3}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone has scored five rows for two ways of answering one question, timed both, written one trust line, and declared no winner.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 5 minutes. The lab page open at part 3. Your two tool windows from the demo, still open on your shared screen, for anyone who cannot open a second option.

**Clock.** 0:00 ask both the same question. 1:00 fill the grid and time each. 3:30 write the trust line. 4:10 chat vote on the first row. 4:40 time.

**Watch for.** A horse race: this is one run of one question, not a benchmark. The nicer formatting winning. A second option that will not open: switch to another of the three, or follow your shared screen; they still fill in the grid.

**Bridge.** "Time. Back together for the debrief: what worked, and what to keep."
:::

## Ask both the same question {#p3-ask}

- Choose a general clinical question from your own field, with no patient details.
- No question in mind? The lab page has a default.
- Ask both in two tabs, with the [evidence-question](../reference/prompt-library.qmd#p-evidence-question) prompt. For a plain literature search, type the key terms.

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 1 min]{.tag} Ask both the same question. [Lab page, part 3](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#part-3)
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Same question, two ways of answering. A general assistant writes from what it learned in training; the second option shows sources you can open. Use whichever of the three you can open today. Choose a general question from your own field, one you can judge, with no patient details. Nothing in mind? The lab page has a default. Paste the evidence-question prompt into both, in two tabs; for a plain literature search, type the key terms.

**Do.** Say "go" and let the countdown run. Anyone who cannot open a second option follows your shared screen and still fills in the grid.
:::

## Fill the grid, then one line {#p3-grid}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Score each row Yes, Partly or No, for both.
- Time each, from asking to a usable answer.
- Then one line: which would you trust, and for what?
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.card .teal}
[What good looks like]{.t}

Five rows scored, both times recorded, one trust line, no winner declared.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 3 min 10 sec]{.tag} Fill the grid. [Lab page, the grid](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#part-3)
:::

::: {.move .chat}
[Chat · 30 sec]{.tag} Type your Yes, Partly or No for the first row, for each tool.
:::

::: notes
**3:40.** Read each answer against the five rows and score it Yes, Partly or No: cites sources you can open, states its limits, answers your question rather than a nearby one, makes claims you could verify, and the minutes to a usable answer. For a plain literature search, mark the rows that do not apply n/a. Then one line: which would you trust, and for what? This is one run of one question, not a benchmark. Do not conclude that one tool is better; conclude what each lets you check. If time allows, open one cited source and see whether it says what the sentence claims.

**Do.** At 4:10 on the part clock, ask for the chat vote. Read out the pattern for the first row; name no winner.
:::

# Debrief [5 min]{.time} {#debrief}

::: notes
**Goal.** Every participant can name one prompt they are keeping and the line they check in its output.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 5 minutes. The lab page open at the debrief. Module 1's slide "What the tool does, what you do" in a tab, for the close.

**Clock.** 0:00 chat: the one prompt or change that worked best, and why; give 90 seconds. 1:30 two or three unmute and say more. 3:30 add it to the personal library. 4:30 close.

**Debrief prompts.** Which of the four parts made the most difference for you, and how do your numbers show it? What was the most confident thing you could not check, or found wrong? Which of the three questions was hardest to answer, and why? In the face-off, which tool did you open first, and what would you still check? What is the one line you check in the output of the prompt you are keeping?

**Watch for.** A result read as a percentage better: there is no such number. A quiet chat: read your own answer first. Probe five trusted because it sounded sure: that is the lesson.

**Bridge to Day Two.** "Tomorrow we take these habits into real documents: notes, audiences, slides and teaching. Bring your favorite prompt."
:::

::: notes
**3:30.** Everyone gets the same question: which prompt, or which change to a prompt, worked best today, and why? Chat first: give ninety seconds for one or two sentences, then read out three or four. Then two or three unmute and say more; use the debrief prompts in the topic notes to draw people out. Keep each answer to a sentence or two, so that three people fit in the two minutes.

**Do.** Click once for the chat move and once for the speak move. If nobody unmutes, read the best chat answers aloud yourself.
:::

- One entry per prompt: a title, the prompt, and the line you check.
- Keep `lab1-practice-output` for Lab Three.
- Bring your favorite prompt to Day Two.

**Good looks like:** you can name the prompt you are keeping and the line you check in its output.

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 1 min]{.tag} Add your entry. [Lab page, debrief](../day1/lab1-templates-and-limits.qmd#debrief)
:::

::: notes
**1:00.** Add the prompt you are keeping to a personal library: a note on your phone or laptop, one entry per prompt, with a title, the prompt with brackets where the facts go, and the line you check in its output, every time. The course's own collection is the prompt library: copy from it, change the facts, and keep your own version. Two things for tomorrow: keep your lab1-practice-output note, because Lab Three uses it, and bring your favorite prompt to Day Two. Then close on the rule: AI drafts. You decide.

**Do.** Paste the lab page and prompt library links in the chat. Say the bridge to Day Two.
:::

## If it goes wrong {#fixes}

| Problem | Fix |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Second option will not open | Use another of the three, or a shared screen. Nothing depends on one. |
| No assistant account | Follow a shared screen. You still fill the grid. |
| "I found nothing to fix" | Reread the plan lines against Case A: doses, the rechecks, the swelling. |
| The tool declines the probe | A good answer. Note it, push once, then try another probe. |
| A real patient detail | Stop, remove it, go back to Case A. |
| Phone only | The lab page works on a phone. Use its stopwatch and notes app. |

::: notes
**Not timed.** Keep this slide for questions, and come back to it when the chat fills with the same problem. Two fixes are not on the slide. Part 1 running over by two minutes: shorten question two's independent check in part 2 from two minutes to one; never cut the save step, which Lab Three needs, or the debrief. Someone re-prompted in Round B: have them record the first draft first, and re-prompt after the lab. If a real patient detail turns up in a chat: no shaming; say the privacy line once: no patient identifiers into a consumer AI tool, ever, full stop.

**Do.** Answer in the chat in one line; share your screen only if a step needs showing.
:::
